> **Simulated data.** All concentration–time profiles are model-generated.
> Physiological parameters (organ volumes, blood flows) are from published
> ICRP reference values. No compound-specific in-vivo data are used.

## Background

Physiologically-based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) models replace empirical PK
compartments with anatomically defined tissue spaces and organ blood flows.
This structure allows mechanistic extrapolation to special populations —
children, renally impaired patients, pregnancy — where empirical PK is rarely
available. A minimal PBPK model retains only the organs most relevant to
distribution and elimination, keeping parameters identifiable.

## Question

Does a minimal PBPK model (lung, liver, kidney, adipose, rest compartments)
with allometric clearance reproduce adult human IV PK? And what oral dose does
a 6-year-old (25 kg) child require to match adult AUC?

## Model

**Compartments:** venous blood, lung, liver, kidney, rest
**Flows:** allometric cardiac output and organ fractions from ICRP (1994)
**Elimination:** hepatic only (well-stirred liver model, IVIVE from CLint)

$$
Q_C = 15 \cdot BW^{0.74} \quad [\text{L/hr}]
$$

$$
\frac{dC_{liver}}{dt} = \frac{Q_L \cdot C_{art} - Q_L \cdot C_{liv}/Kp_L - CL_h \cdot C_{liv}/Kp_L}{V_{liv}}
$$

Full ODE system in `python/pbpk_helpers.py` (`MinimalPBPK.odes()`).

**Pediatric scaling:**
- Organ volumes: linear with BW (exponent 1.0)
- Blood flows: allometric (exponent 0.74 on cardiac output)
- Hepatic CLint: scaled by liver mass fraction (BW^0.75^)

## Limitations

- Minimal PBPK omits gut, spleen, and muscle compartments; these affect
  distribution kinetics for highly lipophilic compounds.
- CLint is estimated by fitting to one synthetic adult dataset; in practice,
  IVIVE from hepatocyte CLint assays with fu correction is preferred.
- Pediatric ontogeny (CYP enzyme maturation, albumin binding) is not modelled;
  this is the main source of underprediction bias in young children.
- Oral bioavailability scaling (gut-wall metabolism, P-gp efflux) is not
  incorporated; the recommendation is for IV dosing.
- Sensitivity analysis covers CLint and fu only; Kp values (tissue:blood
  partitioning) are fixed from literature and their uncertainty is not propagated.
